recommendation: Do not adopt Claude's sequence or sealing text as written. Retain the useful target principles—an immutable archive, a small derived design tree, link-only artifacts, explicit standing, source-complete citations, and per-page adversarial review—but repair the integrity model first. Run disposable pilots and safe read-only checks outside `docs/`; after the owner's preconditions and option choices are resolved, measure a known pre-seal commit and independently review that measurement outside the subtree it measures; make the user's seal the last COORD heading while citing that already-known commit and measurement, without trying to cite the seal commit or an in-tree all-files manifest; make the next commit a pure `git mv docs docs-sealed` with no front door, archive README replacement, packet import, or other addition; then create the new `docs/` front door, an external manifest of `docs-sealed/`, and the derived pages in later commits. Keep the literal prospective `docs/v2/implementation/` path, use a distinct COORD-form successor register for authoritative post-seal decisions, and leave historical ADRs as derived summaries rather than mixing them with new authority.
rationale: The byte inventory substantially holds: the stated rule yields 26 contract companion pages, 32 artifact rows with 31 contract/corpus artifacts after excluding `dr117-ee-gate-naming.v3`, 32 gate pages, 28 final occupancies, 43 directly reachable named corpora, and 49 editorial ADR groups over the packet's 72 BINDING-DESIGN classifications; the baseline page arithmetic is 127. The present file-08 condition table and the 729/760 dispatch split also reproduce. Those correct counts do not validate the execution plan. The proposed manifest must include itself and COORD while COORD embeds the manifest digest; the proposed seal also embeds a commit hash whose commit would contain that hash. The proposed rename commit cannot be rename-only because `docs/README.md` already moves to the archive path while the packet replaces that same path and adds a new front door. A controlled repository test also shows that sibling-directory `git mv` carries untracked files with the directory, directly refuting the orphan premise. Claude additionally relies on an overbroad reading of D-033, uses D-010 to justify a mapping act that D-010 did not perform, proposes importing an unsealed root packet directory into the sealed archive, and would silently change D-000's authoritative-register rules while the draft negates such an amendment. These are structural defects, not small drafting amendments, so the correct verdict is DISAGREE even though several option positions independently remain sound.

refutations.evidence: The table at packet lines 118–158 contains 26 distinct contract-bearing register rows and 32 artifact rows. All 32 named final artifacts exist and their recomputed sha256 values match the table. Excluding the one condition-4 naming artifact `dr117-ee-gate-naming.v3.json` leaves 31 contract/corpus artifacts, exactly as packet line 120 defines; DR-115, DR-119, and DR-123 are decision-only rows and are not artifact rows.

refutations.evidence: File 08 has exactly 32 `DR-G01`–`DR-G32` rows at lines 337–368. COORD has 28 matching non-CONTESTED occupancy recording headings in D-208–D-235; all 28 packet-named occupancy files exist, all 28 sha256 values match, and their own bytes read `status: CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED` and `reviewStatus: AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW`. refutations.claim: The current occupancy/join graph names 43 distinct corpora.
refutations.evidence: The 43 names at packet line 213 are unique, all 43 files exist, all 43 carry top-level `CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED`, and a direct string-reference sweep over the 28 final occupancies plus the 21 current join roots reaches every listed name. `permission-leftover-join.v12.json` separately names 14 permission corpora; `doctor-actor-leftover-join.v12.json` names 13 doctor corpora, one of which is already in the 43, leaving the stated 26 additional distinct files.

refutations.claim: The ADR and total-page counts are 49 groups over 72 BINDING-DESIGN entries and 127 baseline pages.
refutations.evidence: Under the inventory's explicit editorial classification, its 72 listed D-ids are unique, every id resolves to a non-CONTESTED COORD heading, and the group column has 49 distinct values; D-056 and D-133 are correctly one successor-policy group. The proposed-page sum is `4 + 7 + 26 + 32 + 6 + 49 + 3 = 127`. The 72 classification is an inventory rule, not a token present in COORD, so the count holds only under that stated rule.

refutations.claim: The five-condition state and dispatch counts quoted by the recommendation match the current bytes.
refutations.evidence: File 08 lines 414–418 read, respectively, MET, NOT MET with 5 of 32, MET, MET with 32 owners and 28 named required gates plus 29 OPEN/3 HARD-BLOCKED, and NOT MET. Independent filesystem/Git counts return 729 tracked `_dispatch.*.txt` files, 760 on disk, and 31 untracked.

refutations.claim: D-010 supplies the same mechanism for either 5-C or the fallback 5-B mapping-only clause.
refutations.evidence: COORD D-010 lines 1003–1012 says C-D010 amended file 08 itself to the range-free condition-2 wording and appended a historical pin-note at lines 119–121; the register is operative. That is precedent for a reviewed pre-seal file-08 edit such as 5-C, not for leaving file 08 unchanged while a later seal merely maps its words as 5-B proposes.

refutations.claim: D-033 establishes a record-wide `path + digest` convention supporting link-only JSON.
refutations.evidence: COORD D-033 lines 1815–1824 expressly limits its subject to DR-001 citation form and certain rows citing the same way; its form is `(path, named section or selector, segment hash)`, not a general full-file path-plus-sha256 rule. Link-only remains preferable on independent single-source and drift grounds, but Claude's cited precedent is overbroad.

refutations.claim: A final user-made seal plus independently reviewed measurement is in the established form.
refutations.evidence: D-000 lines 20–25 is a direct user-made protocol entry; D-054 lines 2361–2376 and D-132 lines 5554–5563 expressly record later user decisions verbatim while requiring separate D-000 cycles for later named acts. That supports a reviewed measurement followed by a distinct user seal, provided the measurement and integrity references are non-circular.

refutations.claim: `seal-manifest.v1.json` can live under `docs/` and contain one path plus sha256 for every tracked file under `docs/`, while D-SEAL in COORD cites the manifest digest.
refutations.evidence: Packet lines 478–483 put the manifest at `docs/coop/artifacts/seal-manifest.v1.json` and require every tracked file under `docs/`. Once tracked, the manifest must hash itself. It must also hash COORD, while COORD's D-SEAL bytes contain the manifest's sha256. Neither exclusion is stated, so the prescribed bytes have self- and cross-referential digest dependencies and cannot be generated by the proposed procedure.

refutations.claim: D-SEAL can state `sealed at HEAD <X>` where `<X>` is its own C-DSEAL commit.
refutations.evidence: Packet lines 465–483 put `<X>` inside D-SEAL, and archive-README line 559 identifies `<X>` as the C-DSEAL commit. A Git commit id depends on the tree containing COORD and therefore on the `<X>` bytes inside COORD; editing in the resulting id creates a different commit id. A seal entry can cite an already-known parent/baseline commit, but not its own not-yet-existing commit hash.

refutations.claim: The rename commit can both be a byte-identical, renames-only move and add the packet's archive README plus a minimal new `docs/README.md`.
refutations.evidence: `docs/README.md` is already a tracked file. `git mv docs docs-sealed` therefore creates `docs-sealed/README.md` containing those existing bytes. Packet lines 540 and 546–562 simultaneously add a new front door and prescribe different content at that occupied archive path. The commit must contain an addition and, if the archive draft is used, an overwrite; it cannot show renames only or zero content changes.

refutations.claim: `git mv` leaves untracked files behind at the old path, so the 31 dispatch texts would be orphaned.
refutations.evidence: In a controlled temporary Git repository with one tracked and one untracked file under `docs/`, `git mv docs archive` produced `R  docs/tracked.txt -> archive/tracked.txt` and `?? archive/untracked.txt`; both files moved and the old directory disappeared. In the packet's command sequence, the subsequent `git add -A <ARCHIVE>` would stage such files rather than leave them orphaned.

refutations.claim: Moving root `DECISION-PACKETS/` into `<ARCHIVE>/packets/` in the rename commit preserves the sealed archive and the rename-only property.
refutations.evidence: `DECISION-PACKETS/` is outside `docs/`, is not covered by the proposed docs manifest, and `git ls-files DECISION-PACKETS` returns no tracked packet files at this HEAD. Importing it under the archive would add unsealed bytes that were never members of the moved `docs/` tree and would make the archive larger than the byte-identical source tree.

refutations.claim: The D-SEAL draft's negation that it does not amend D-000 remains true with Claude's option 6.10(a).
refutations.evidence: D-000 lines 3–12 and clauses 3–4 at lines 36–42 require delegated decisions in this register, in its entry form, with per-decision commits. Claude would close that register, end the D-NNN series, and put new authoritative decisions among derived ADRs. Packet D-SEAL lines 507–520 both authorize a successor location and say D-000 is not amended except for closure. The location, identifier/form, and authority changes are substantive D-000 amendments and must be explicit.

refutations.evidence: The pilots sample one contract page, one gate page, and one ADR, while the 127-page baseline also contains root, register, design, index, and glossary work with different source density. Three observed cycles can expose template defects and provide three samples, but cannot replace or validate the heterogeneous 16–28-day estimate that packet line 663 already labels unmeasured.

amendments: Replace the circular seal manifest with an independently reviewed measurement of an already-known pre-seal commit/tree. Do not put an all-tracked-files manifest inside the subtree it hashes, and do not embed the seal commit's own hash in D-SEAL. After the pure move, a manifest outside `docs-sealed/` may hash every archived file, including the terminal COORD bytes.

Use separate commits for the terminal user seal, the pure directory move, and creation of the new front door/derived tree. Keep `docs-sealed/` byte-identical; put seal metadata, path mapping, and the actual seal/rename commit references in the new front door or a sibling metadata file, not by replacing the moved archive README.

Scope the pre-seal path-mapping rule to tracked paths that actually existed in the sealed tree. Preserve the absent prospective `docs/v2/implementation/` path literally; authorization to create it does not require creating a stub during the rewrite. If the owner instead selects a different live path, use a reviewed pre-seal file-08 amendment in the 5-C form rather than claiming 5-B is the D-010 mechanism.

Use a separate COORD-form authoritative successor register and continue with the next unused D-series identifier measured at that time unless the owner expressly amends D-000's identifier scheme. Keep the 49 historical ADRs derived and non-authoritative. D-SEAL must state the D-000 amendment to register location and closure explicitly.

Give the 26 DR-join-named corpora one canonical catalog on the DR-105/DR-114 row pages because those row joins name them; let G09/G12 cross-reference that catalog. This preserves the exactly-one-home rule without inventing ownership.

Amendment A is useful as a disposable template/pre-check pilot, not as replacement estimation. Record only the three observed cycles and preserve DR-104's policy-versus-unapplied-artifact distinction.

Amendment B should begin only with read-only inventory, citation, digest, and ledger validators. Defer the manifest generator and mapping rewriter until the seal scope, exclusions, prospective-path rule, and archive name are fixed.
Replace amendment C with: 127 is a provisional baseline for the stated option set; the effort range remains unmeasured, and the pilots provide samples rather than a ceiling or project-wide estimate.

optionPositions.6.1: Recommend (b) `docs-sealed/`: it communicates immutability better than `docs-old/`. The owner still chooses the name once; keep the archive a sibling, not a self-nested tree.
optionPositions.6.2: Recommend (a) link only. Use the archive as the sole byte home and independently specified full sha256 checks; do not rely on D-033 as a repository-wide convention because D-033 is narrower.
optionPositions.6.3: Recommend (b) 49 ADR groups under the packet's stated classification, with a complete D-NNN-to-ADR reverse map and every member's negations retained. Treat these ADRs as derived summaries, not new authority.
optionPositions.6.4: Recommend (b) include candidates, conspicuously labelled `CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED` and `binds NOTHING`, with row status shown separately. Do not assume that most candidates will necessarily change standing before the seal; derive standing from the eventual sealed bytes.
optionPositions.6.5: Recommend the literal treatment in 5-A, amended so it does not prematurely create a directory: limit archive mapping to paths present in the sealed tree and preserve the prospective absent `docs/v2/implementation/` path exactly. If a different live path is genuinely desired, 5-C is the faithful D-010-style route; do not use 5-B as a substitute precedent.
optionPositions.6.6: Recommend (a) link fixture and corpus bytes. Give the join-named corpora one canonical row-page catalog under DR-105/DR-114 and cross-link from G09/G12; do not list them as two homes.
optionPositions.6.7: Recommend (c) in two distinct acts: independent adversarial review of a measurement pinned to an already-known pre-seal commit, followed by the owner's verbatim terminal seal. The seal must not self-pin its commit or an in-tree circular manifest.
optionPositions.6.8: Recommend (a) for the 31 dispatch texts only after verifying their intended provenance content, because a sealed archive should not carry an untracked overlay—not because `git mv` would orphan them. Do not move root `DECISION-PACKETS/` into the archive or include that move in the pure docs rename commit.
optionPositions.6.9: Recommend (a) pointers only. Keep V1 authority byte-exact in the archive and avoid expanding the rewrite into a second narrative project.
optionPositions.6.10: Recommend (b), a distinct COORD-form authoritative successor register. Continue the actual D-series with the next unused identifier measured at the time, retain D-000 review/reversibility/commit fields, and keep condensed historical ADRs separate from live decisions.
